overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: no evidence of outside deliberation, and the chair lawfully limited public comment, though public participation was encouraged.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a quorum of the Board colluded outside a meeting to reach its decision on continuing health insurance coverage for elected officials.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that the Board deliberated outside of a meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board took action on a matter without allowing public comment at its February 22 meeting, when the chair declined to take comment before the vote.
allegations.key_passage: It is within the Chair's discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, and thus he did not violate the Open Meeting Law by doing so here.
